comments.content: Require a nonzero time delta (and unchanged center) for this purely vertical center-track drag. The current condition accepts a center-only change, after which `baseDragDelta` is zero; if the second drag also fails to move time, the scroll-speed comparison accepts zero versus zero. This allows both the temporal-drag and per-note-speed checks to pass when temporal dragging is broken.

comments.content: These assertions do not observe audio continuity: the stage advances `_second` from frame delta independently of the audio player, and `playing=True` reports `_playing`, not the player's playback position. Stopping/restarting the audio during an incremental update would therefore still pass this check. Add stage telemetry for the actual player position and a restart/load counter, then verify playback remains aligned and no restart occurs across this edit.

                    !window.LastStageInput.Contains("selection=1", StringComparison.Ordinal) ||

comments.content: Check the complete geometry after undo, not only width. Resizing one edge changes both `Center` and `Width`, so an undo that restores width but leaves the center shifted passes this assertion and leaves subsequent native gestures operating on the wrong geometry. Assert the original time, center, and width together after this single undo.
comments.existing_code: if (window.CurrentDocument?.SelectedChart.Notes.Single(note => note.Id == "fixture-note").Width != 1)

comments.content: Disabling the chart audio override after browsing for a replacement still installs that replacement. The dialog retains `_chartAudioSource` when the checkbox is unchecked and submits both a source and `ClearChartAudio = true`; this code gives the source precedence and suppresses clearing. Honor `ClearChartAudio` before scheduling a replacement (or omit the source from the dialog request when disabled), so the resulting chart inherits package audio as requested.

The replacement retains the old package filename even when the selected audio has a different format. For example, replacing `audio.wav` with an OGG stages OGG bytes at `audio.wav`. `ReplaceChartResourceCommand` does not transcode, and `V2BuiltInAudioProbe` chooses its parser from the package-relative extension, so the next save rejects the replacement although preview can play the external OGG. Derive a suitable destination extension from the new source for both package and chart audio, or explicitly reject format changes before applying settings.

List selection is never written to EditorDocument.Selection, but UpdateView clears both lists and RestoreSelection uses only that document selection. For example, after adding BPM A, clicking BPM B and then refreshing through a chart reorder restores A rather than B; with no timing document selection, the selected row disappears altogether. Synchronize user timing selections with the document (and clear the other timing list), or preserve the panel's selection independently during refresh.

The same time fields serve both Add and Apply, so making them read-only for the base event also blocks entering an insertion time. This occurs automatically after adding the initial bar-zero Scroll event: it is selected on refresh, the time field becomes read-only, and Add keeps submitting zero and fails as a duplicate. Provide a separate new-event/deselection action or separate insertion fields; the core commands already prevent moving the base event.

Snapping and clamping each selected note independently changes the group's relative timing and spacing. Off-grid notes can receive different time deltas, and dragging two notes toward a stage edge moves the boundary note less than the other one. NudgeSelection has the same behavior. Compute one snapped time delta and one position delta constrained by the whole selection, then apply those shared deltas to every selected note.

comments.content: These three-decimal display values are now submitted as authoritative geometry by ApplyGeometry. Opening an existing note with higher-precision center/width and changing only its bar time silently rounds both geometry values; even clicking Apply without edits changes the note. Display round-trip precision for editable values, or retain the original values when their fields have not been edited.

comments.content: Moving `Rect2.Position` leaves its `Size` unchanged, so dragging the center-track start edge translates the entire ghost instead of stretching it with the opposite edge fixed. The side-track `else` branch has the same problem. Preserve the original opposite corner and recompute the size after moving the grabbed edge, so the resize preview matches the committed resize.
comments.existing_code: if (moveStartEdge) rect.Position = new Vector2(rect.Position.X + delta.X, rect.Position.Y);

comments.content: Playback commands do not respect the new pan-suspension flag: `SetPlaying(true)` always clears `StreamPaused`, while this condition still freezes the preview clock. Pausing and resuming with the keyboard during an active playing pan therefore lets audio advance while the chart remains frozen until release. Make playback transitions preserve pan suspension (and ensure seek/restart paths do not start audio during it).
comments.existing_code: if (!_panAudioSuspended) _second += delta * _playbackRate;

comments.content: Six fixed-point iterations do not reliably invert even a continuous, increasing scroll ramp. For example, with BPM 120, currentSecond=0, and scroll increasing linearly from 1 at bar 0 to 10 at bar 1, a point projected from bar 0.5 resolves to approximately bar 0.386 after these iterations. Placement and drag coordinates therefore drift substantially on valid charts. Use a bounded root solver against the forward distance function (with an explicit policy for multiple solutions/discontinuities), and add round-trip tests for steep ramps.
comments.existing_code: for (var iteration = 0; iteration < 6; iteration++)

comments.content: Apply the release position to the width draft before committing or calling BeginTail. Currently only motion events update the width; a press/release sequence with no delivered motion commits the initial width, and a dropped final motion commits a stale width. For Hold/Mixer, the subsequent UpdatePlacement runs after TailStage is enabled, so it updates only the tail and permanently freezes the stale head width.

comments.content: The snapping predicate differs from SnappedBarAt, which disables snapping whenever Z is pressed. With Ctrl+Z held, the ghost uses an unsnapped time but labels it as snapped and sends Snap=true; ShellChartEditor.PlaceNote then snaps it again, placing the note at a different time from the ghost. Use the same modifier predicate for coordinate resolution and the preview/request flag.
comments.existing_code: var snap = !Input.IsKeyPressed(Key.Z) || Input.IsKeyPressed(Key.Ctrl);

comments.content: Existing-note alignment markers omit the note's ScrollSpeedMultiplier when calculating its position. The stage renderer includes this multiplier, so notes with non-unit speed receive squares at a different position (or are incorrectly culled). Include note.V2Metadata?.ScrollSpeedMultiplier ?? 1 in this distance calculation while retaining unit speed for the new placement ghost.
comments.existing_code: var remaining = RemainingFor(track, note.Second, note.BarTime, metadata);

comments.content: Resource changes applied to an unsaved draft are not included in its first save. These commands stage sources in `Document.PendingResourceReplacements`, but `EditorDocumentSession.Save` uses `Draft.BuildPackageCreateRequest` for an unpersisted document, which only includes the draft's original `ExternalResources`. Replacing package audio therefore previews the new source but saves the old one; adding a cover or chart audio override can instead fail because its resource mapping is missing. Merge pending replacements into the first-save mappings (with pending sources taking precedence), or reject resource changes on drafts until that path supports them.

A package without preview metadata acquires a 15-second preview merely by opening settings and applying an unrelated edit: `BuildRequest` always submits these values and `Apply` installs them when the original preview is null. For valid audio shorter than 15 seconds, this also makes the next save fail the resolved-preview duration check. Preserve the absence of a package preview unless the user explicitly enables/edits it, rather than treating the display fallback as authored metadata.
comments.existing_code: var packPreview = document.Preview ?? new V2Preview(0, 15);

comments.content: Snapping the width after ResizeFromEdge while retaining span.Center moves the supposedly fixed opposite edge. For example, center 2 and width 1 with the end edge dragged to 2.6 produces center 2.05/width 1.1; snapping that width to 1 moves the start edge from 1.5 to 1.55. Recompute the center from the original opposite edge and the snapped width so edge resizing preserves its anchor.
comments.existing_code:
var width = EditorStagePlacement.SnapWidth(span.Width);
            var center = Math.Clamp(span.Center, width / 2d, 5 - width / 2d);

comments.content: Loading an existing BPM into BpmValueInput silently clamps values outside its XAML range [1,999], although EditBpmCommand accepts any finite positive BPM. Selecting a valid 1200-BPM event and changing only its time therefore saves it as 999. ScrollValueInput has the same problem for valid scroll values below its minimum of 0.05. Make the input ranges match the core domain or preserve unchanged values rather than submitting the clamped display values.
comments.existing_code: this.FindControl<NumericUpDown>("BpmValueInput")!.Value = (decimal)bpm.Bpm;

comments.content: The same screen-space delta does not represent the same chart edit on every track. For example, when a center-track and side-track note are selected, dragging the center note vertically changes time; the side note should move horizontally along its travel axis, but this ghost moves it vertically. Notes with different scroll multipliers also need different travel distances. The shell applies shared bar/center deltas to the group, so the notes jump away from these previews on release. Derive the gesture's chart-time/center deltas and project each member through its own track and scroll geometry instead of translating every rectangle by the raw pointer delta.
comments.existing_code: : new Rect2(rect.Position + delta, rect.Size);

comments.content: Resize hit-testing uses the rendered edge, but the release converts that pixel position directly to a logical chart edge. Those edges are not equivalent: rendered center-track widths are scaled by 0.95, and side-track widths use 102 × 0.95 pixels per unit rather than the 115 used by CenterAt. For example, dragging the right edge of a width-5 center note outward by 10 pixels actually shrinks it, because the initial rendered edge is already about 34 pixels inside the logical edge. Preserve the grabbed-edge offset and apply the pointer delta to the original logical edge (with the appropriate visual-width scale), rather than treating the absolute pointer coordinate as that edge.
